title: Hennessy’s in downtown Boston has closed, plans to transfer liquor license to new Seaport restaurant
author: Samantha Genzer
bullets: Hennessy's Bar in downtown Boston closed after nearly 30 years, marking its final day on Tuesday.
The bar plans to transfer its liquor license to Bar 23, a new Seaport restaurant opening next year.
Hennessy's, known for Irish food and live music, was a six-time "Best Irish Bar in Boston" winner.

title: Framingham remote Logan terminal will be extended through March
author: Madison Lucchesi
bullets: MassPort's remote Logan terminal in Framingham will continue operation through March, serving 10,000 passengers since the June 1 launch.
Delta and JetBlue passengers can use the Framingham remote terminal for TSA screening and baggage check before heading to Logan Airport.
MassPort aims to expand remote terminals to other locations and include more airlines; tickets can be purchased 90 days in advance.

title: Sonny Gray reportedly interested in signing extension with Red Sox
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Sonny Gray is interested in a contract extension with the Boston Red Sox beyond the 2026 season.
Gray, currently 12-2 with a 2.78 ERA, has been the team's most reliable starter this season.
Boston's rotation, featuring young pitchers, could benefit from Gray's veteran presence after his standout performance.

title: Teen driver killed, 4 others hospitalized in stolen SUV crash in Abington
author: Samantha Genzer
bullets: A 17-year-old driver died in a stolen SUV crash in Abington, authorities confirmed.
Four teens, aged 14 to 17, were hospitalized with severe injuries after the crash on Washington St.
The crash occurred while police attempted a traffic stop on the stolen Hyundai Santa Fe.

title: Celtics ‘expressed interest’ in LeBron James in free agency before he joined 76ers
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: The Boston Celtics showed interest in signing LeBron James as he entered free agency after leaving the Lakers.
LeBron James ultimately signed a two-year deal with the Philadelphia 76ers for the veteran's minimum, prioritizing championship contention.
The Philadelphia 76ers now feature a lineup including James, Jaylen Brown, Joel Embiid, Tyrese Maxey, and VJ Edgecombe.

title: Parts of Mass. under flash flood warning as state sees heavy rain
author: Madison Lucchesi
bullets: Flash flood warning in effect until 6 p.m. for Western Massachusetts, including Springfield, Chicopee, and Westfield.
Berkshire County faces a flood warning until 5:45 p.m., with potential rainfall up to 7 inches.
Central and Western Mass., Eastern Rhode Island, and Connecticut under flood watch until 8 p.m. due to heavy rain.

title: Cyclist, 39, killed in Stoughton crash
author: Madison Lucchesi
bullets: Mark Salvador, 39, died after a crash with a vehicle on Route 138, Stoughton, early Wednesday morning.
Salvador was taken to a Boston hospital and pronounced dead an hour after the crash.
Police have not released information on any driver involved; investigation by Norfolk County DA is ongoing.

title: Wu unveiled a street safety plan after a cyclist was killed. Transit advocates say it doesn’t go far enough.
author: Samantha Genzer
bullets: Mayor Michelle Wu unveiled a street safety plan after Louisa Gag's death, proposing several city initiatives.
Advocates criticize Wu's plan for lacking specific timelines and accountability, despite pledges to improve safety measures.
Plans include installing quick-build barriers and truck safety legislation, but details on implementations remain vague.

title: What to know about the Green Line shutdowns planned for August
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: MBTA will suspend Green Line service in August for tunnel and accessibility upgrades affecting B, C, D, and E branches.
Free shuttle buses will replace suspended services, with added capacity on the 39 bus for the Green Line E branch.
MBTA advises riders to expect an additional 25 minutes travel time and check mbta.com/PlannedWork for updates.

title: Suffolk corrections officer killed after stopping to help stranded motorist in Boxford
author: Beth Treffeisen
bullets: Brett Martin, 51, a Suffolk corrections officer, was fatally struck on I-95 in Boxford while assisting a stranded motorist.
Massachusetts State Police responded to the scene at 8:30 p.m.; Martin was later pronounced dead at a local hospital.
The Essex County District Attorney’s Office is investigating; Martin served with the Suffolk County Sheriff’s Department since 2008.
